transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, well... I guess what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to actually finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, I do computer support, right? And I'll sit down to start tracing a client's network problem... which, honestly, has been an absolute nightmare this week because of this new router firmware update everyone is pushing. It completely bricked half the enterprise systems we manage. My buddy Dave—we went to grad school together—he called me yesterday just complaining about the exact same patch. He actually brews his own beer now, which is pretty cool. He brought me a stout last month that was... uh, wait. Sorry. What was I saying? 

Right, the network logs. So I'll be sitting there trying to fix this issue, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times in a row, and I still don't know what they say. My brain just completely checks out on me.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with your attention and focus?

Well, the really serious trouble started about... I'd say a year and ten months ago. Yeah, almost two years. That’s when I was fired from my old position. 

At that job, I had all these specific systems in place that kept me on track. I had this whole automated workflow dashboard I built myself using Python. Python is just so much better for that kind of backend scripting than what everyone is pushing now. My nephew is actually learning some new web framework, and I tried looking at his code over Thanksgiving, and it was just a complete mess. We had turkey, but my sister also made this incredible smoked brisket... she leaves it in the smoker for like fourteen hours with hickory wood. I actually wanted to buy a smoker myself after that, but the HOA in my neighborhood is ridiculously strict about what you can put on your patio. The guy who runs it, Gary, he literally walks around the block with a clipboard just looking for violations... 

Wait, sorry. You asked when this started. Right. So, yeah, about a year and ten months ago. When I got fired, I lost all those systems and the structure that was holding my daily routine together, and it's just been impossible to stay on track since then.
Thinking back to when you were a kid in elementary or middle school, did you have trouble with focus or paying attention back then?

Oh, yeah. Actually, my mother still jokes about that. She kept all my old grade school report cards in this big cedar chest at her house. My dad actually built that chest for her... he was a hobbyist carpenter, made some really beautiful furniture using all these intricate dovetail joints. I tried getting into woodworking myself a few years back, bought a bunch of expensive chisels and a Japanese pull saw, but I just ended up cutting my thumb open and bleeding all over the garage floor. I still have the scar right here... 

Wait, sorry. School. Right. 

So she kept the report cards, and she always laughs because every single one of them said the exact same thing. The teachers would write that I was a bright kid, but I never, ever stayed in my seat. And I was always blurting out answers in the middle of class before anyone else could raise their hand. Oh, and I lost my homework constantly. Which was incredibly frustrating because I actually *did* the homework! I'd finish the math worksheet or whatever, and then it would just vanish into another dimension before I got to school. 

Kind of like my car keys now, honestly. I finally bought one of those Bluetooth tracker tags for my keychain, but the battery died on it last week. They use those weird flat coin batteries, and you have to buy a pack of like eight at the pharmacy, and then you just end up losing the other seven anyway... wait, what was the question again? Did I answer it?
Nowadays as an adult, do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or like you have trouble sitting still?

Oh, absolutely. I'm constantly moving. Like, if I'm sitting down with a client to go over their system architecture, or even when I'm at my local chess club... I play chess every Tuesday night, actually. We meet up at this little community center downtown. The parking there is an absolute nightmare, though. They have these meters that only take an app, and the app is so poorly designed. I swear, the UI was thrown together by an intern who doesn't understand basic user flow. I actually emailed the developer about a bug in their payment gateway, but they never responded. Typical. I used to do some front-end dev work back in the late 90s, when everything was just HTML and table layouts. It was simpler then, you know? 

Uh, sorry. You asked about sitting still. Right. 

So yeah, even at the chess club or with clients, my leg is just constantly bouncing under the table. Or I'll be clicking a pen over and over, or just twisting a plastic cable tie around my fingers. I don't even realize I'm doing it until somebody finally gives me that annoyed look, and then I have to force myself to stop. But a minute later, I'm doing it again.
